project.name: PR-Review-Agent-Production-Level
project.objective: Build a production-grade, evidence-driven AI pull-request review system that analyzes PR changes in repository context, runs specialized review agents, aggregates and confidence-gates findings, escalates uncertain or critical decisions to humans, publishes justified findings to GitHub, and records durable evidence for reliability, evaluation, economics, governance, and continuous improvement.
constraints: Develop on develop; main is production-intent only.
Genesis engineering protocol is mandatory during the project lifecycle.
Product implementation is prohibited until Phase 0 specification and planning gates are satisfied.
Existing Multiagent-PR-Review-System is reference material only.
Architecture must remain modular and preserve explicit trust boundaries.
The end-user product is cloud-hosted via a GitHub App; customers do not install or operate our runtime infrastructure.
Provider/model and embedding choices must remain behind replaceable interfaces until evaluation freezes them.
non_goals: Build a generic autonomous coding agent instead of a PR review system.
Add infrastructure solely to make the project appear more production-grade.
Treat LLM output or repository content as authoritative instructions.
Silently promote learned policy changes without measured evaluation and approval.
Require end users to install local workers, databases, queues, runtimes, or model credentials.
project.trust_boundary: GitHub events, PR text, repository contents, retrieved code, tool output, and LLM output are untrusted inputs; privileged actions must cross explicit authenticated and authorized boundaries.

lifecycle.next_action: Create and verify requirement-linked Phase 1 architecture tasks, then present the Phase 1 plan for explicit human approval.

assumptions.statement: GitHub is the first supported SCM/provider integration and the primary review publication surface.
The initial specialist set is security, quality, tests, and documentation.
LangGraph may be used as the first workflow engine implementation behind an internal abstraction.
Tiger Cloud/Postgres-compatible storage is the intended durable data spine, subject to Phase 1/architecture validation.
The customer experience is a hosted SaaS product using a GitHub App; customer-side infrastructure is not required.
Initial target languages are Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Spring Boot, with emphasis on AI/ML and MERN/PERN/modern JS/TS workloads.
Managed container deployment is preferred; AWS ECS/Fargate is an approved candidate subject to Phase 1 verification.
GitHub App installation scope should support both repository/user-oriented and organization/account-oriented flows where practical, with simplification allowed if complexity becomes disproportionate.

invariants.statement: No finding is published without attributable evidence tied to the reviewed change and repository context.
No specialist agent may bypass the finding normalization, aggregation, deduplication, and policy gate.
Untrusted PR/repository content, retrieved context, tool output, and model output must never become implicit trusted control instructions.
Privileged tools must be explicitly scoped, authorized, observable, and least-privileged.
Equivalent webhook delivery must not create duplicate review work or duplicate published findings.
Every production review decision must be attributable to a review run, agent/event lineage, policy state, and evidence.
Low-confidence, critical-impact, or policy-sensitive outcomes must be eligible for human escalation rather than forced publication.
Cost controls must be evaluated before expensive model execution where technically possible.
Evaluation artifacts and evaluators must be protected from modification by the candidate system under test.
Learning or policy changes require measurable baseline/candidate evaluation, independent review, explicit promotion, and rollback capability.
The system must prefer slower-but-correct behavior over fast-but-unjustified review output.
Durable project decisions, requirements, assumptions, and operational knowledge must not exist only in chat history.
Customer repository access must be scoped through the authorized GitHub App installation and application authorization context; dashboard visibility is never sufficient authorization.
The vector dimension is not authoritative until a retrieval benchmark selects the embedding model and compatibility is verified.
Chat-session continuity must be recoverable from repository state without requiring conversational memory.

decisions.statement: The new repository is greenfield; the previous PR-review repository is reference material, not the architectural source of truth.
develop is the construction and verification branch; main represents production intent.
Phase 0 must complete specification and planning gates before product implementation begins.
The production system is designed around explicit evidence, policy, auditability, and human escalation rather than comment volume.
Specialist agents are parallel domain reviewers; the aggregator is the authority for normalized findings and publication eligibility.
LLM strategy is provider-neutral abstraction with one evaluated initial provider/model.
Embedding selection requires a retrieval benchmark before the concrete model and vector dimension are frozen.

GitHub publication is designed for inline review plus a summary/check surface, with a fallback to inline review plus summary if reliable dual publication cannot be achieved without unjustified complexity.
Initial language support targets Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Spring Boot for AI/ML and MERN/PERN/modern JS/TS workloads.
HITL uses GitHub identity with a pluggable application RBAC layer so simpler GitHub-only authorization can be introduced without domain redesign.
Production autonomy is configurable per repository with conservative defaults; autonomy is decided by policy, not by LLM confidence alone.
Frontend is minimal and capability-driven rather than speculative.
Customer experience is cloud SaaS via GitHub App; customer-side runtime infrastructure is not required.
Large PRs use staged/degraded review with explicit limitations and human-directed multi-pass review where required.
Managed container deployment is preferred; AWS ECS/Fargate is an approved deployment candidate subject to verification.
GitHub App installation scope aims for both user/repository-oriented and organization/account-oriented flows, with fallback to a simpler model if combined complexity becomes disproportionate.
The repository must contain an explicit cross-chat handoff protocol and checkpoint artifact so a fresh session can recover the exact project state.

knowledge.statement: The end-user deployment model is a hosted GitHub-native SaaS: browser login, GitHub App installation/authorization, repository selection, cloud review execution, and GitHub-native publication.

Embedding vector dimension is a derived parameter that follows the selected embedding model after retrieval benchmarking and compatibility verification; prior fixed-dimension planning examples are non-authoritative.
CONTINUE-HERE.md is a session handoff artifact. Canonical authority remains Genesis state plus approved specification/architecture artifacts.

discovery.reference_policy: reuse ideas only after explicit requirement, impact analysis, and verification
